newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH RAPESEED CROP SEEN HITTING RECORD 3 MLN TNS.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH RAPESEED CROP SEEN HITTING RECORD 3 MLN TNS.

text.p: France's SIDO oilseeds association, revising up its key rapeseed estimate by some 120,000 tonnes, predicted on Monday the crop would hit a record above three million tonnes this year.
In its first annual estimate in early July, SIDO had forecast French rapeseed output of 2.88 million tonnes, about in line with the previous year's 2.87 million.
"For 1997 French production should exceed three million tonnes and English and German crops should be at comparable levels to 1995," SIDO said in a published review of the last three seasons.
It did not give figures for those countries but noted that in 1996 France's 40 percent share of European Union output had been unusually high because of poor German yields that year.
SIDO said at the time of its previous 2.88 million estimate that this year's French yields were expected to fall 10 percent, which would be more than offset by an 11 percent rise in area.
Its new report gave no updated yield projections.

It projected a 1997 French sunflower crop of between 1.9 and 2.0 million tonnes, close to last year's harvest of two million tonnes and potentially higher than its own previous forecast of 1.9 million tonnes.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture in mid-July forecast total European Union rapeseed output of 8.13 million tonnes, up from 7.14 million tonnes in 1996.
